quiz.q: What defines India as a 'soft state' according to Gunnar Myrdal's Asian Drama?
options: Its limited capacity to effectively enforce laws and implement policies despite passing comprehensive legislation.
Its lack of formal administrative institutions and bureaucratic structures inherited from colonial rule.
Its total subservience as a clientelist puppet regime serving foreign metropolitan capital.
Its complete subordination of civilian institutions under an authoritarian military oligarchy.
quiz.why: Myrdal defined a soft state as one that passes laws but suffers from poor implementation and weak enforcement capacity.

quiz.q: According to Hamza Alavi, how does the post-colonial state relate to social classes?
options: It serves strictly as an instrument of the indigenous capitalist class against foreign competitors.
It acts as a relatively autonomous mediator among three competing propertied classes.
It represents exclusively the economic interests of the traditional indigenous feudal class.
It operates purely as a direct instrument of the metropolitan bourgeoisie alone.
quiz.why: Alavi argued that the post-colonial state mediates between three competing classes: the metropolitan bourgeoisie, indigenous bourgeoisie, and indigenous feudal class.

quiz.q: Why did Hamza Alavi describe the state in post-colonial societies as 'overdeveloped'?
options: The indigenous capitalist economy developed much faster than the political superstructure.
The state successfully eradicated all feudal relations through comprehensive land reforms.
Colonial rulers established an advanced administrative apparatus over a society that remained traditional.
Political parties established complete democratic oversight over the inherited colonial bureaucracy.
quiz.why: The state is overdeveloped because modern administrative machinery was imported by colonizers into an economically and socially traditional society.

quiz.q: In F.W. Riggs's model of prismatic societies, what is meant by 'formalism'?
options: The dominance of modern constitutional rules over traditional customs in daily life.
The harmonious integration of distinct ethnic communities into a single national identity.
The complete alignment of market pricing with state-subsidized canteen goods distribution.
A substantial discrepancy between enacted laws and rules and their actual practical implementation.
quiz.why: Riggs defined formalism as a large gap between theory (formal laws and regulations) and practice (how administration actually operates).
